concepts.title: Event and Sample Space
concepts.definition: A specific outcome or a collection of outcomes from a random experiment that corresponds to a subset of the sample space.
concepts.key_idea: Events are represented as subsets of the universal set of outcomes.
question_patterns: define an event in probability

solution_steps.explain: List all possible outcomes of the random experiment as set S.
Select outcomes from S that satisfy the specific condition of the event.
Group the filtered outcomes into a set E, which is a subset of S.

concepts.title: Simple and Compound Events
concepts.definition: An event is simple if it contains only one outcome, and compound if it contains multiple outcomes from the sample space.
concepts.key_idea: Classification based on the number of sample points in the event set.
question_patterns: is the event simple or compound
identify the simple events in the sample space

classify the following events
how many simple events are possible for this experiment

solution_steps.explain: Identify all sample points that belong to the event set E.
Determine the cardinality n(E) of the event set.
If n(E) is 1, it is simple; if n(E) is greater than 1, it is compound.

concepts.title: Mutually Exclusive Events
concepts.definition: Events that cannot happen at the same time, meaning their intersection is an empty set.
concepts.key_idea: Disjoint sets in the context of probability where occurrence of one prevents the other.
question_patterns: check if events A and B are mutually exclusive
are these events disjoint

solution_steps.explain: Identify outcomes common to both event A and event B.
Verify if the intersection set contains any elements.
If the intersection is empty, the events are mutually exclusive.

concepts.title: Exhaustive Events
concepts.definition: A collection of events whose union covers the entire sample space, ensuring at least one of them must occur.
concepts.formula: E1 union E2 union ... union En = S
concepts.key_idea: The set of events accounts for every possible outcome in the experiment.
question_patterns: are the events exhaustive
verify if the union of events equals the sample space
do these events form an exhaustive set
check if at least one of these events must happen
determine if the given events cover all outcomes

solution_steps.explain: Combine all outcomes from the given set of events into a single union set.
Check if the union set is identical to the sample space S.
If the union equals S, the events are exhaustive.

concepts.title: Axiomatic Probability Validity
concepts.definition: Rules requiring that probabilities are non-negative, the total probability of the sample space is one, and the sum of probabilities of disjoint outcomes equals one.
concepts.key_idea: Mathematical constraints for a valid probability assignment.
question_patterns: is the assignment of probabilities valid

solution_steps.explain: Ensure every individual probability is between 0 and 1 inclusive.

concepts.title: Classical Probability Calculation
concepts.definition: The probability of an event in a sample space where all outcomes are equally likely to occur.
concepts.key_idea: Ratio of favorable outcomes to the total number of possible outcomes.

concepts.title: Addition Rule for Probability
concepts.definition: The probability that at least one of two events occurs is the sum of their individual probabilities minus the probability of their joint occurrence.
concepts.formula: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
concepts.key_idea: Adjusting the sum of probabilities by subtracting the overlapping intersection.
question_patterns: find the probability of A or B
calculate the chance of at least one event occurring

find the probability of opting for NCC or NSS

solution_steps.explain: Add the probability of event A and the probability of event B.
Subtract the probability of both events occurring from the sum.

concepts.title: Complementary Event Probability
concepts.definition: The probability that an event does not occur is found by subtracting the probability of its occurrence from one.
concepts.key_idea: The sum of probabilities of an event and its complement is always one.
question_patterns: find the probability of not A
calculate the chance that event A does not occur
what is the probability of the complement of A
determine P(A') given the value of P(A)
if the probability of an event is p, find the probability of its non-occurrence

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the probability of the event from the total probability of 1.

concepts.title: Probability of Event Difference
concepts.definition: The probability of event A occurring without event B is the probability of A minus the probability of the intersection of A and B.
concepts.formula: P(A but not B) = P(A) - P(A and B)
concepts.key_idea: Removing the joint occurrence from the probability of the primary event.
question_patterns: find the probability of A but not B
calculate the chance that only event A occurs
what is the probability of A intersection B-prime
determine the likelihood of Anil qualifying but not Ashima
find the probability of opting for NSS but not NCC

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the probability of both events from the probability of event A.

concepts.title: Probability of Exactly One Event
concepts.definition: The probability that exactly one of two events occurs, calculated by summing the probabilities of each event occurring alone.
concepts.formula: P(exactly one) = P(A) + P(B) - 2 * P(A and B)
